A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Similarity-Dissimilarity Loss research. All pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including v4 Appendices A–F. v2 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments on MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV and MS-COCO in Tables 2–4 and Figure 2.

after.justification: v4 reports original image and text classification results in Tables 1–2, with medical classification results in Appendix E and Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The proposed loss and similarity/dissimilarity factors in Equations (13)–(15) remain unchanged, as does encoder training followed by classifier training with a frozen encoder. The corrected relation definitions and newly documented architecture details do not establish a changed loss procedure.

E1.justification: v4 retains MS-COCO and all six MIMIC settings while adding PASCAL VOC, NUS-WIDE and AAPD. This substantially broadens image coverage and adds scientific-abstract classification beyond v2's medical text evaluations.

E2.justification: ALL, ANY and MulSupCon remain the comparator losses throughout the corresponding evaluations. Backbone changes concern experimental configurations. JSPCL and MSC enter related-work discussion but are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Medical evaluation drops CNN, BERT, ELECTRA, XLNet and BioBERT and adds Llama-3.1-8B with LoRA, retaining RoBERTa and PLM-ICD. Reported text-training scheduling changes from linear scheduling with 1e-4 warmup to cosine scheduling with 0.05 warmup. MS-COCO splits change from approximately 83k/41k/41k to 82k/20.2k/20.2k, and mAP replaces P@1 in image evaluation. These are reported setting changes, not proof that particular experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's MIMIC distribution and ICD-9 comparisons, v4 adds descriptive analyses of relative micro/macro-F1 gains and cross-method score dispersion across image datasets and text encoders (Figures 2–3). These examine modality and label-cardinality effects, without introducing controlled component ablations or robustness sweeps.

E5.justification: v2 reports point estimates only. v4 adds standard-deviation and distribution summaries across the four loss methods in Figures 2b and 3. These are descriptive cross-method statistics, not repeated-run uncertainty; neither version reports seeds, run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds results for the new datasets and Llama, expands MIMIC-IV-ICD9-Full and top-50 result reporting, and removes results for five backbones. MS-COCO results are replaced: the proposed method's micro/macro-F1 changes from 70.2/65.3 in v2 Table 4 to 73.40/70.03 in v4 Table 1. The revised settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: v2 Propositions 2–4 survive as v4 Theorems 1–3, with their proofs expanded and moved to Appendix A. Substantive additions are Theorems 4–5 and their proofs, establishing conditional ordering of R3 versus R4/R5 weighting factors. Equations (11)–(12) also change containment to strict containment, separating these relations from equality.

C1.justification: The central assertions remain five label-set relations, similarity/dissimilarity-based loss adjustment, and improved classification relative to the same three losses across text and images. v4 foregrounds theoretical support and adds broader evidence, but v2 already asserts mathematical support and cross-modal effectiveness.

C2.justification: v4 interprets larger macro-F1 gains as evidence of long-tail efficacy and explains smaller PASCAL/text gains through label cardinality and pretraining. It expands discussion of Llama and domain-specific knowledge. v2's explicit limitations concerning supervision, batch size, augmentation and unaddressed label co-occurrence are removed; v4 instead discusses nonlinear/learnable weighting, while Appendix E acknowledges persistent extreme-tail difficulty.

D1.justification: v4 Appendix D newly specifies hardware, temperature, the 256-dimensional two-layer projection head, linear BCE classifier, LoRA parameters, precision and additional optimizer details, and supplies a code-access link. Conversely, it omits v2's explicit batch sizes, token-length search, image-augmentation recipe and early-stopping rule. These are substantial documentation changes, with both additions and losses.

R1.justification: Appendix F extends the similarity-only comparison to JSPCL and MSC and adds Jaccard-related context. Additional citations support the new datasets, Llama/LoRA and medical-LLM discussion, while references associated with dropped encoders disappear. The central positioning against overlap-based contrastive losses remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, results and conclusion, and adopts MSCL terminology. Proofs, experimental details, medical results and related work are reorganized into Appendices A–F, while image and general-text results become the main narrative. The author and affiliation block also changes.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. Figure 1 is retained, but medical curves and the improvement table give way to consolidated appendix tables, including rotated full-page tables. New image gain/dispersion plots, AAPD boxplots and substantially reorganized dataset/result tables alter the presentation beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v4 provides a limited net improvement through broader nonmedical evaluation, corrected containment definitions and substantially more implementation detail. Reduced encoder breadth and omitted settings temper these gains. The expanded proofs establish label-factor properties, but Equation (13) still places label-only multipliers inside the logarithm, so they do not reweight representation gradients for a fixed positive set; the claimed theoretical effectiveness remains unresolved.
